title: Exponential speedup of polarization stabilization for long distance DWDM quantum networks
authors: Jinyi Du, En Teng Lim, Xingjian Zhang, Hongwei Gao, George F. R. Chen, Dawn T. H. Tan, Alexander Ling
abstract: Fibre-based quantum networks distributing polarization entanglement require a stable and uninterrupted transmission basis for reliable operation. Bright classical reference light enables rapid polarization feedback but can introduce noise into quantum channels. Entangled-photon-based feedback avoids this noise, but typically interrupts the target entanglement channel during calibration and becomes prohibitively slow over long distances due to the product loss of fibre links. Here, we overcome both limitations by combining wavelength-bracketed probing with switch-enabled path decomposition. Spectrally adjacent entangled-photon sidebands track the polarization response of the central distribution channel without interrupting its transmission, while optical switches and local reference fibres independently determine the signal and idler network transformations. Transferring the resulting compensation settings to the central channel eliminates calibration-induced downtime and changes the acquisition-time scaling from the product of the link losses to the sum of losses. We demonstrate the method on a 133 km fibre testbed and achieve continuous closed-loop stabilization for more than 24 hours without classical reference light. The decomposition of multi-link quantum feedback into single-link measurements provides a scalable stabilization strategy for wavelength-multiplexed quantum networks.
summary: This paper presents a novel technique to stabilize polarization entanglement in long-distance quantum fiber networks by combining wavelength-bracketed probing with optical switching. This approach overcomes the limitations of previous methods by eliminating downtime and changing the acquisition time scaling from the product to the sum of link losses. The method successfully demonstrates continuous, high-fidelity stabilization over extended periods.
main_problem: Maintaining stable polarization basis is crucial for reliable, long-distance quantum networks distributing polarization entanglement.
main_result: The proposed method achieves continuous closed-loop stabilization for over 24 hours without classical reference light, demonstrating a scalable strategy for multi-link quantum feedback.
method: The authors combine wavelength-bracketed probing with switch-enabled path decomposition to decouple the polarization stabilization measurement from the central quantum channel.
model_or_system: The system is a fibre-based quantum network distributing polarization entanglement in a Dense Wavelength-Division Multiplexing (DWDM) configuration, utilizing entangled-photon sidebands and optical switches.
key_observables: Central channel entanglement fidelity (e.g., 95.1%), coincidence-to-accidental ratio (CAR), and the polarization transformation matrix (Stokes vector evolution).
important_parameters: Link lengths (e.g., 133 km), loss rates ($\eta_s, \eta_i$), and the scaling of acquisition time (from product-of-losses to sum-of-losses).
main_assumptions: The local reference fibre loss is assumed negligible compared to the network fibre losses, and a first-order approximation is used for the wavelength-bracketing technique.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the spectral allocation of sidebands bracketing the central channel, the switching mechanism using WSS, and the continuous, stable evolution of the Stokes vectors over time.
paper_structure: The paper first identifies the limitations of existing feedback methods (noise from classical light, slow acquisition time scaling). It then introduces the two-stage decoupling strategy: using sidebands for non-interruptive probing, and using switches to decompose the joint measurement into independent single-link measurements, culminating in experimental demonstration and fidelity measurements.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the engineering challenges of scaling quantum communication networks by providing a robust, noise-free, and time-efficient method for polarization stabilization, which is a critical component of quantum networking.
